comparison: Both evaluate platform design and characterization (C1, C16-C19) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on technical validation via SEM and stiffness measurements. Peer review emphasizes the platform's value for throughput and consistency. Peer review also includes C54 (main findings summary) not in OpenEval R1.

Both address cell ratio optimization (C2, C21-C22, C24). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED based on tissue stability data. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN due to concerns about only 50% survival at 20 days, questioning whether optimization is truly complete despite authors' responses.

Perfect agreement on structural organization claims (C3, C25-C30, C74-C75). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes extensive immunofluorescence evidence and 3D reconstruction. Peer review notes good sarcomere striation and convincing morphology demonstrations with no specific critiques.

Both evaluate contractile function development (C4-C5, C31-C34, C36) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on quantitative temporal data and statistical significance. Peer review includes C23 and C77 (spontaneous beating) and affirms appropriate methodology for proof-of-concept validation.

Both address live imaging with voltage-sensitive dye (C39-C40, C42). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with acknowledged technical limitations (noisy repolarization). Peer review rates SUPPORTED after initial concerns about geometry-induced arrhythmia were resolved by voltage dye demonstrations showing no arrhythmia in miniaturized tissues.

Perfect agreement on calcium dose-response experiments (C7, C43-C44, C66). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes EC50 determination with confidence intervals and literature validation. Peer review accepted data as part of concordant inotropic responses without specific critique.

Perfect agreement on verapamil dose-response (C7, C45-C47, C67). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes IC50 determination and literature validation, with minor formatting concern in confidence interval. Peer review accepted as expected inotropic response with IC50 in expected range.

Both address isoproterenol response (C7, C48-C49, C79-C80) but with different assessments. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveats about unexpected response pattern and hypothesis about immaturity. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, noting inconsistency with typical positive chronotropic/inotropic responses and other reported results, representing unresolved discrepancy.

Both evaluate dofetilide arrhythmogenic effects (C8, C50-C53). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED emphasizing dose-dependent reduction and Poincaré analysis. Peer review rates SUPPORTED after initial concerns, confirming platform correctly detected pro-arrhythmogenic effects under spontaneous beating. Peer review includes C83 (spontaneous beating limitation).

Perfect agreement on differentiation efficiency (C20). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes flow cytometry data showing >96% efficiency consistent with optimized protocols. Peer review implicitly accepted this methodological detail without questioning.

Both address spontaneous contractile activity (C23, C77). OpenEval R11 rates SUPPORTED with video evidence and longitudinal data. Peer review R4 includes these claims within broader contractile function evaluation, also rated SUPPORTED as part of platform validation.

Both address pillar stiffness and reproducibility (C18-C19). OpenEval R1 includes these in platform characterization rated SUPPORTED. Peer review R11 specifically addresses reviewer concerns about pillar consistency, rating SUPPORTED after authors demonstrated reproducible Young's Modulus with low standard deviations via AFM.

Partial overlap on contractile parameters (C6, C34). OpenEval R4 rates temporal development SUPPORTED with statistical significance. Peer review R5 rates force measurement methodology UNCERTAIN, accepting the approach but noting suboptimal variability (standard deviation quarter of value) despite high replicates.

Partial overlap on performance benchmarking (C59-C60). OpenEval R13 rates comparisons to native tissue SUPPORTED with appropriate literature citations. Peer review R5 addresses force measurement methodology concerns, rating UNCERTAIN due to measurement variability issues despite accepting the overall approach.

Both address fluorescence imaging compatibility (C57). OpenEval R5 includes this in live imaging capabilities rated SUPPORTED. Peer review R13 specifically validates this capability through voltage-sensitive dye experiments that addressed arrhythmia detection concerns, rated SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on platform limitations (C81-C82, C84-C85). Both rate SUPPORTED. OpenEval R17 honestly acknowledges limitations as consequences of miniaturization and design choices. Peer review R14 accepts these as reasonable trade-offs for high-throughput format, noting pharmacological responses were correctly measured under spontaneous beating.

OpenEval R12 summarizes main findings (C54-C56, C58) rated SUPPORTED by collective experimental evidence. Peer review R1 includes C54 in platform validation, emphasizing value for throughput and consistency. Both affirm overall platform capabilities.

OpenEval R12 includes C55 (tissue stability) in main findings summary rated SUPPORTED. Peer review R2 questions tissue stability with only 50% survival at 20 days, rating optimization claims UNCERTAIN. Divergent assessments of stability achievement.

OpenEval R14 evaluates design advantages and potential applications (C71-C73) as SUPPORTED based on demonstrated capabilities. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific interpretive claims about design benefits.

OpenEval R15 evaluates claim C76 (recapitulation of native tissue organization) as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about two-cell-type limitation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing this interpretive claim.

OpenEval R16 evaluates calculation about conduction wave detection (C78) as SUPPORTED based on tissue dimensions and known conduction velocities. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this technical calculation.

OpenEval R18 evaluates background context claims (C9-C15) as SUPPORTED with appropriate literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviews typically focus on novel findings rather than background knowledge claims.

OpenEval R19 evaluates methodological context and literature support (C63-C65, C69-C70) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these methodological justification claims.
